hook: 溜 has the water radical: water that pools and collects (たまる) in one place.
黙 is black (黒) plus dog (犬): a black dog sitting silent in the dark, saying nothing.
Words (言) plus a formula (式): you test an idea by trying it out.
Water (氵) you collect on purpose: ためる is to save up, like a tank you fill.
散 means scatter: ちらす is to scatter things around on purpose, like throwing paper everywhere.
散 means scatter: cherry blossoms scatter and fall (ちる) from the tree.
捕 has the hand radical: a hand catches the thief, so he gets caught (つかまる).
掴 has the hand radical (扌): your hand grabs and grasps something tight.
Attach (付) plus fit together (合): people who stick together keep company with each other.
就 means take up a position: you settle into a job or a seat (就職 is getting a job).
突 means thrust: you poke or strike forward suddenly, like 突然 (suddenly).
次 means next: つぐ is to come next, to rank right after someone.
着 means wear (着る): つける is to put something on, like a mask or a seatbelt.
繋 has thread (糸) at the bottom: things tied with thread become connected (つながる).
Thread (糸) ties things: つなぐ is to tie or connect, like holding hands (手をつなぐ).
Thread (糸) joins things: つなげる is to connect one thing to another.
詰 means pack or cram: you pack things tightly into a box until it is full.
積 means pile up: snow piles up (雪が積もる) little by little.
適 means suitable (適当, 適切): てきする is to suit or be right for something.
Pass through (通り) plus go past (過ぎる): to walk right past a place without stopping.
溶 has water (氵): you mix paint or powder into water so it dissolves.
退 means retreat: どく is to step back and get out of the way. どいて means move!
Water (氵) appears when ice melts: とける is to melt or dissolve.
飛 means fly: you make something fly past, so you skip over it (とばす).
Fly (飛) plus out (出): to fly or rush out suddenly, like a cat jumping out.
留 means stop or fasten: you fasten something so it stays in place.
泊 means stay overnight (一泊 is one night): とめる is to let a friend stay the night.
Take (取り) plus up (上げる): pick something up, or a teacher takes your phone away.
取 means take: とれる is when something comes off by itself, like a loose button.
亡 means dead or gone (死亡): なくす written this way is to lose a person to death.
鳴 is mouth (口) plus bird (鳥): make a bell sing like a bird, to ring it.
為 means do or purpose (ために): なる, to become or change into something.
生 means life and grow: a tree grows and bears fruit (実が生る).
馴 has horse (馬): a wild horse slowly gets used to people and becomes tame.
煮 has fire dots (灬) at the bottom: food on the fire boils and gets cooked.
握 has the hand radical (扌): grip with your hand, like making an onigiri (おにぎり).
抜 means pull out: ぬける is when something comes out or falls out, like hair.
濡 has water (氵): to make something wet, to soak it.
乗 means ride (乗る): のせる is to let someone ride, or put something on top.
覗 has see (見): you secretly look in through a small gap, to peek.
除 means remove (掃除 is cleaning): のぞく is to take something out, to exclude.
延 means extend or prolong: のばす is to make something longer, like a deadline.
伸 means stretch: のびる is to stretch out or grow, like a child getting taller.
延 means prolong (延長 is extension): のびる here is when time or a date gets longer.
述 means state: のべる is to say your opinion clearly, as in a speech or essay.
昇 has the sun (日) on top: the sun rises and goes up (日が昇る).
載 means load or print (記載): your name rides (のる) on the page, so it appears in print.
生 means grow: grass, hair or a baby's teeth grow and spring up (はえる).
量 means quantity: はかる is to measure how much, to weigh it.
吐 is mouth (口) plus earth (土): something comes out of your mouth onto the ground, to throw up.
外 means outside: はずす is to take something off and put it outside, like glasses.
外 means outside: はずれる is to come off or miss, to end up outside the target.
罰 means punishment (罰金 is a fine): ばっする is to punish someone.
離 means separate (距離 is distance): はなす is to move things apart.
放 means release (放す): はなれる written this way is to break free and get away.
Flow (流) plus go (行): a fashion that flows and goes everywhere is popular.
Pull (引) plus stretch (張): to pull hard and drag something along.
冷 means cold: ひやす is to make something cold, like putting a drink in the fridge.
広 means wide: ひろがる is to become wider, to spread out.
広 means wide: ひろめる is to make something widely known, to spread it.
深 means deep: ふかまる is to become deeper, like a friendship or autumn.
拭 has the hand radical (扌): your hand wipes the table with a cloth.
含 has a mouth (口) under a lid: something held inside the mouth, so it contains it.
含 means contain: ふくめる is to include something, to put it in the group.
吠 is mouth (口) plus dog (犬): a dog opens its mouth and barks.
Tiny (微) plus laugh (笑): a small laugh, a gentle smile.
巻 means roll or scroll: まく is to wind or roll something, like a scarf or sushi roll.
蒔 is grass (艹) plus time (時): at the right time you sow seeds for plants.
撒 has the hand radical (扌): your hand throws water or seeds all around, to scatter.
混 means mix (混雑 is crowded): まざる is when things get mixed together.
交 means cross or mix (交差点 is a crossing): different things mix but stay separate.
混 means mix: まじる is to be mixed in, like water and paint blending.
交 means cross: まじる here is to mingle, like one person mixed into a crowd.
増 means increase (増える): ます is to grow more, to gain.
交 means cross or mix: まぜる is to mix things in, like cards in a deck.
裂 has clothes (衣) at the bottom: cloth that rips and splits open.
沿 has water (氵): you walk along beside a river, following its line.
高 means high: たかまる is to become higher, to rise, like hopes or tension.
摘 has the hand radical (扌): your fingers pick flowers or tea leaves.
強 means strong: つよまる is to become stronger, like wind or rain.
強 means strong: つよめる is to make something stronger, to emphasize it.
問 is a mouth (口) at a gate (門): someone at the gate asks a question (問題).
説 means explain (説明 is explanation): とく is to explain or preach an idea.
綴 has thread (糸): you bind pages together with thread, or file papers.
慣 means get used to (慣れる): ならす is to make someone used to something.
馴 has horse (馬): you train a horse so it becomes tame.
臨 means face or be present (臨時 is temporary): you face the sea, or attend an event.
映 has the sun (日): sunlight makes things shine and look beautiful.
諮 has words (言): you use words to ask others for advice, to consult.
図 means plan or drawing (地図 is map): はかる is to plan or try to achieve something.
生 means grow: はやす is to let something grow, like a beard.
広 means wide: ひろまる is when news spreads widely by itself.
深 means deep: ふかめる is to make something deeper, like your knowledge.
経 means pass through (経験 is experience): へる is to pass through time or places.
See (見) plus hang (掛ける): something catches on your eyes, so you happen to see it.
捲 is hand (扌) plus roll (巻): your hand rolls back pages, to turn them over.
弱 means weak: よわまる is to become weaker, like a storm dying down.
弱 means weak: よわめる is to make something weaker, like turning down a fire.
